newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
LALOO YADAV QUITS, HIS WIFE IS NEW CHIEF MINISTER

Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav quit his post on Friday and his wife Rabri Devi was sworn in as the new Chief Minister along with 13 ministers. Laloo Yadav stepped down after a designated Central Bureau of Investigation court issued arrest warrants against him. His wife was then elected as the leader of the ruling Rashtriya Janata Dal party. Shortly after Laloo Yadav's resignation on Friday afternoon, the Supreme Court stayed his arrest till July 29. Laloo Yadav told reporters that he had resigned as chief minister because he did not want to create a constitutional crisis following the issuance of arrest warrants against him.
The Hindustan Times
NARAYANAN SWORN IN AS NEW PRESIDENT

K.R. Narayanan was sworn in as the 10th president of India on Friday at a ceremony in the Central Hall of Parliament. He pledged to fight corruption, communalism, casteism and violence. He recalled Mahatma Gandhi's observation in 1948 that indifference to matters like corruption was criminal and regretted that despite Gandhi's caution corruption was widespread in the country. Narayanan was administered the oath of office and secrecy by the chief justice of India. He took the oath in Hindi in the name of god. Immediately after taking the oath Narayanan and outgoing President Shankar Dayal Sharma exchanged seats.
The Economic Times
EXPORT PROMOTION BOARD SET UP

The government set up an export promotion board to take decisions on all export-related issues with the aim of enhancing exports. The board will be chaired by the cabinet secretary and will have secretaries from the ministries of commerce, finance, textiles, surface transport, agriculture, revenue, civil aviation and the departments of electronics and industrial policy. The board will try to improve export competitiveness by addressing cost-related elements that hinder exports.
FIAT TO BUY ENTIRE DOSHI STAKE IN PALIO VENTURE

Italian car major Fiat SpA is buying the entire 24 percent stake of the Doshi family in its 30 billion rupee Palio world car joint venture. With this Fiat will have a 100 percent stake in the company. The Doshis' Premier Automobiles will have an option to buy back up to 49 percent of the stake from Fiat after three years. They can also acquire a stake through an issue of shares. The Doshis are selling their stake because they are facing a financial crunch and are unable to fund the project. The buyback option has been given to them to participate in the project when it commences production. Fiat is setting up the Palio car project in Maharashtra state to manufacture 100,000 cars a year.
AIRCRAFT ACT TO BE RECAST

The Civil Aviation Ministry set up a sub-committee to revamp the Aircraft Act of 1934. It is headed by the joint secretary of civil aviation and have members from the ministries of law and industries. The sub-committee was set up following a suggestion by the director general of civil aviation that the 60 year old law be scrapped and be replaced by a new one to catch up with the new environment in the civil aviation sector. The Aircraft Act governs the entire civil aviation sector giving wide procedural and administrative powers to the director general of civil aviation.
Financial Express
GILTS CRASH ENDING BULL RUN IN SECONDARY DEBT MARKET

Gilt prices crashed by 15 paise to 25 paise in the secondary debt market on Friday, ending a frenzied bull run. The crash came after prolonged overheating in the securities market which led to gilt prices going up and yields tumbling. Bankers said the hike in yields of some of the securities was the first indication that interest rates were realigning themselves at a more realistic level. The securities whose prices crashed include the 11.83 percent gilts maturing in 2003 which were auctioned this week, the 12.59 percent gilt maturing in 2004, the 11 percent gilt maturing in 2002 and the 13.50 percent gilt maturing in 1998.
MAURITIAN FIRM PICKS UP STAKE IN TWO INDIAN FIRMS

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) allowed Asian Telecommunication Investment of Mauritius to pick up equity stakes in two telecommunication companies of the Usha Martin group. It will pick up 49 percent of the equity in UMTL Holding Company of the Usha Martin and nine percent equity in the Usha Martin Telecom. The Mauritian company will make strategic investments in the Indian telecom sector and software developments. The FIPB also allowed the DDS Mobile company to change one of its overseas joint venture partners.
Business Standard
RESERVE BANK PREDICTS DIP IN INTEREST RATES

Reserve Bank governor Chakravarty Rangarajan on Friday predicted a nine percent rise in capital expenditure by corporates for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) and indicated a further fall in interest rates. Monetary policy will be generally supportive in bringing down the interest rates, he said. The Reserve Bank governor said since the inflation rate remained at a reasonably low level and inflationary expectations were broken it should be possible to bring down the nominal interest rate.
BANKS MAY SLASH SHORT TERM DEPOSIT RATES

Government banks are planning to cut their short term deposit rates to maintain spreads in the face of a massive liquidity overhang. The move follows a build-up of deposits and poor credit offtake. The banks have already cut deposit rates once when the Reserve Bank slashed the bank rates by 100 basis points last month. For the last two months a few banks were selectively cutting short term deposit rates of large deposits.
FIRMS PLAN TO ADOPT AMERICAN DEPOSITARY RECEIPTS

At least 15 Indian companies are planning to adopt the American Depositary Receipt (ADR) route to get listed on the National Association of Securities Dealers' Automated Quotes (Nasdaq) from the first quarter of 1998. A team from Nasdaq will visit India this September to discuss the listing norms with software and telecom companies. Nasdaq Stork Market Asia-Pacific business development director said key Indian companies in the telecom, software, auto parts, pharmaceuticals and infrastructure sectors could be listed on the exchange next year.
The Observer
RESERVE BANK PANEL TO REVIEW COMMODITY HEDGING

The Reserve Bank Friday appointed a committee to go into issues related to hedging against price risk through international commodity exchanges. The terms of reference of the committee includes the identification of the important export/import commodity groups where price volatility affects Indian corporates and where such risks can be hedged on recognised international commodity exchanges. It will also examine the nature and extent of legal impediments which bar the recourse of Indian entities to international commodity exchanges and find ways to overcome them.
